considered.reasoning: Every archived signal treated financing as a net amount (raise vs return); this one holds the amount roughly aside and asks which security was chosen, a channel that neither CMA nor the net-issuance factor prices directly. The financing leg is winsorized and z-scored so it is centered, letting the smoothed cash-profitability rank act only as an amplitude gate, which keeps the construct non-monotone in profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Payout Policy Innovation Gated By Cash Profitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 3)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Markets have long since learned the level of a firm's net payout; the priced information is the innovation — a cash-profitable firm moving to a distribution posture materially above its own recent norm is revealing newly confirmed surplus cash, while a cash-profitable firm suddenly turning into a net raiser is revealing a funding need or a valuation the managers wish to exploit.
considered.reasoning: Demeaning net external financing by the firm's own three-year average makes the financing leg orthogonal to the static net-issuance and payout anomalies that likely explain why gen-0 level interactions had strong Fama-MacBeth slopes but near-zero FF5 alphas. This is the corrected version of the gen-1 proposal rejected for lacking a financing-exclusive variable, now built from actual repurchase, dividend, and issuance flows rather than the clean-surplus identity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Verified Cash Generation With Verified Distribution
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), sstk), 3), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Underpriced cash generation requires both facts to be true at once over a multi-year window: the firm must actually have produced cash from operations, and it must actually have handed cash back net of new equity; either alone is uninformative, since debt-financed distributions and hoarded cash flow are both common.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the ratio-with-ABS-denominator by a MIN of two industry-standardized three-year flows removes the pathology the critic identified — a cash-burning firm now scores at its (very negative) cash-flow z-score no matter how much debt-financed cash it distributes, so it cannot enter the long leg. It also stops being a payout-ratio variant: the score is the weaker of two independently measured cumulative flows, which is a conjunction rather than a quotient, and both legs remain continuous with no point mass.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Flow Coverage Of Short Term Debt
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Debt in current liabilities is the balance of financing that must actually be refinanced or repaid within the year; firms whose normalized operating cash flow exceeds that obligation are insulated from credit-market conditions and can distribute freely, whereas firms whose near-term obligations dwarf internal cash are rollover-dependent and exposed to funding shocks the market underweights in calm periods.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that dltr is realized debt reduction rather than scheduled maturities; dlc is the actual stock of short-maturity obligations, so the revised expression measures rollover exposure rather than penalizing deleveraging. Smoothing operating cash flow over three years makes the coverage measure reflect normalized earning power rather than a single year's working-capital swing, and the bounded [-1, 1] form keeps cash-burning firms pinned near the floor.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profitable Firms Reducing Leverage Ratio
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm with established operating profitability that is lowering the share of its balance sheet financed by outside claims is converting operating strength into financial independence, whereas an equally profitable firm whose liability share is rising is funding something its reported profits cannot cover, or is levering to sustain payouts.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the share-count leg the critic flagged as a rediscovery of composite issuance (and as split-contaminated) and substitutes the change in the liabilities-to-assets *ratio*, which is not asset growth: a firm can grow assets rapidly and still lower its liability share by funding growth internally. It preserves the original motivation of testing whether the archive's weak ls_talpha reflects sample breadth, since oiadp, lt and at are near-universally reported, while the centered financing leg keeps the composite non-monotone in profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Worst Year Funding Independence
considered.expression: TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(sstk, dltis))), 3)
considered.hypothesis: Financial independence is defined by the bad years, not the average year: a firm whose *worst* recent year still saw operations supply most of its funding never had to accept the market's terms, and this tail property of the funding mix is what distinguishes genuinely self-sufficient cash generators from firms that merely look self-funded in good years.
considered.reasoning: This is not an average of the archived level and trend signals but a different order statistic of the same underlying cross-theme ratio — a minimum rather than a mean or slope — and it encodes a distinct economic claim about tail dependence on capital markets that neither prior signal can express. Firms with one bad capital-raising year are demoted regardless of a flattering three-year average, which specifically separates chronic self-funders from cyclical ones and should sharpen the long leg where the archive's funding-mix signals earned their positive Sharpe.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Service Capacity After Interest Burden
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(oibdp, 3), xint), ADD(ABS(MA(oibdp, 3)), ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Operating profit left over after paying the cost of existing debt, measured against the stock of debt itself, is the market's slowest-updating measure of solvency; firms generating ample post-interest profit per dollar of debt have capital-structure slack that supports future distributions, while firms whose profits are consumed by interest are effectively working for creditors.
considered.reasoning: This shifts the coverage mechanism from a cash-timing question (can I repay maturing principal?) to a price-of-capital question (does the business out-earn its financing cost?), using the interest expense channel that no archive signal has touched. Because oibdp, xint, dltt and dlc are income-statement and balance-sheet items rather than cash-flow-statement flows, coverage should exceed the roughly 0.09 typical of the prstkc/sstk constructs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Generative With Long Dated Debt
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, ADD(ADD(dlc, dltt), 1))), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Financial autonomy requires both a cash engine and a debt structure that does not force the firm back to the market soon; the maturity *composition* of debt, independent of how much debt there is, determines how often management must submit to credit-market conditions.
considered.reasoning: This separates the scale of obligations (already captured by the gen-2 coverage ratio) from their maturity mix, testing whether short-dated funding structure is a distinct risk channel rather than a proxy for having too much debt relative to cash. The MIN enforces the conjunction the hypothesis states — a firm cannot enter the long leg on cash flow alone or on long maturities alone — and both legs are continuous industry z-scores, avoiding the point masses that destabilized the indicator constructs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Leveraged Dividend Payers
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvt, ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A dividend that consumes a large share of internally generated cash is only safe on an unlevered balance sheet; when the same payout sits on top of heavy debt, the firm has pre-committed nearly all of its cash flow and any operating shortfall forces either a dividend cut or distressed financing, so these firms should underperform equally distributing but unlevered firms.
considered.reasoning: Every archive payout construct treated distributions as unambiguously good news about cash generation; this asks when the same distribution is instead evidence of over-commitment, interacting payout intensity with the leverage stock rather than with issuance flows. The payout-intensity rank sets amplitude only and the centered leverage z-score sets the sign, so the signal is not monotone in either theme and its short leg is specifically the fragile levered payer.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stress Year Coverage Of Near Term Debt
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(TS_MIN(oancf, 3), dlc), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Refinancing risk is realized in bad years, so what matters is whether the firm's *worst* recent year of operating cash flow would still have covered its near-maturity debt; firms that pass this stress test never have to approach credit markets from weakness, while firms that pass only on average are one bad year away from dilutive or distressed financing.
considered.reasoning: Rather than adding a small, collinear dividend term to the archive's best coverage ratio, this replaces the central-tendency measure of cash flow with a tail statistic, which is a different economic claim: two firms with identical three-year average coverage are now separated by the volatility of their cash generation relative to their funding calendar. The change is attributable — any improvement over the parent is due to downside cash-flow risk interacting with near-term obligations, not to a rescaling of the same two quantities.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maturity Extension By Cash Generators
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, ADD(ADD(dlc, dltt), 1)), 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Managers of cash-generative firms who shift their debt from short to long maturities are deliberately buying insulation from credit-market conditions, typically because they can borrow long cheaply and see no need to keep re-opening the funding question; the opposite shift, toward short-dated debt, usually reflects lenders shortening tenor on a deteriorating credit, which the equity market recognizes late.
considered.reasoning: This is a corporate *action* on the liability side (the change in maturity mix) rather than a first difference of the archive's coverage level, so a null result is informative about whether maturity management carries information distinct from the level of funding autonomy. The maturity-mix change is self-normalizing — it is a share, not a dollar amount — which avoids the dlc scale noise that would have dominated a differenced coverage ratio, and the centered financing leg keeps the composite non-monotone in profitability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Unusual Borrowing Relative To Own Norm
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dltis, at), MA(RATIO(dltis, at), 3)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Chronic borrowers (leasing-like capital structures, serial refinancers) are already priced; the informative event is a cash-generative firm borrowing far more than its own recent norm, which reveals a funding need not visible in its cash-flow statement — an acquisition, a working-capital deterioration, or a payout it cannot self-fund.
considered.reasoning: Demeaning debt issuance by the firm's own three-year average removes the level component that constitutes the documented external-financing anomaly, so a firm that always issues 10% of assets in debt now scores zero and only deviations from its financing routine are ranked. This is therefore not a sign-flipped decomposition of the gen-2 pecking-order signal but a test of borrowing *surprise*, and because the financing leg is centered, the cash-profitability rank sets only the amplitude of the response rather than the direction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding Autonomy With Revealed Distribution
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Capital returned to shareholders is credible evidence of underpriced cash generation only when the firm is not simultaneously obliged to the credit market; a distribution from a firm whose maturing debt exceeds its operating cash flow is a transfer from creditors, whereas a distribution from a firm with funding autonomy is genuine surplus.
considered.reasoning: The archive shows a sharp split — coverage-type signals produce reliable FF5 alpha (5.2% at t=3.68) while net-payout constructs produce strong Fama-MacBeth slopes but almost no alpha — and the natural diagnosis is that unconditional payout is spanned by RMW/CMA while payout backed by funding autonomy is not. MIN enforces the conjunction so a firm cannot enter the long leg on coverage alone or payout alone, which directly tests whether the payout theme adds anything once the funding-obligation state is controlled.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rising Cost Of Debt Despite Operating Profits
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(xint, ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Interest expense per dollar of debt is the price creditors charge the firm; when that implied rate rises for a firm that still reports healthy operating profitability, informed lenders are repricing risk that the equity market has not yet recognized, while a falling implied rate for a profitable firm signals improving creditworthiness that will later show up in equity valuation.
considered.reasoning: No archive signal has used the price of capital — only its quantity — so this tests whether credit-market pricing information leads equity returns, a genuinely different channel from coverage or payout. The financing leg is a centered change in a rate, so it is orthogonal to the level of leverage and to asset growth, and oiadp, xint, dltt and dlc are all widely reported, giving coverage in the 0.12 range achieved by the gen-3 interest-burden signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistent Coverage Of Near Term Obligations
considered.expression: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, dlc), 0), 5), RANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that has covered its near-term debt out of operating cash in every one of the last five years has demonstrated structural funding independence, whereas a firm that covers today but failed twice recently is a cyclical borrower whose current coverage will not survive the next downturn; the market prices the current state and underweights the track record.
considered.reasoning: The archive's coverage family has been tested only as a current level, a tail, and a change, never as a frequency, and the frequency statistic captures a different economic property — reliability of the funding position across states of the world. Multiplying the 0-5 count by the continuous current-coverage rank supplies a within-bucket tiebreaker, avoiding the lumpy decile boundaries that plausibly produced the perverse Sharpe of the gen-0 count construct and the null gen-1 signed count.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Internally Funded Debt Retirement
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The clearest evidence of underpriced cash generation on the debt side is a firm that both produces strong operating cash and uses it to retire more debt than it raises; such firms shrink creditor claims on future cash flow without any market transaction, whereas cash-generative firms that keep rolling debt forward are recycling rather than earning.
considered.reasoning: The theme's "return capital" idea has been tested almost entirely through the equity channel (buybacks, dividends, share issuance); this is its debt-channel counterpart, and paired with Signal 1 it tells us whether conditioned capital return works through repaying creditors, through paying shareholders, or both. Using dltr as a *use of internal cash* rather than as a proxy for scheduled maturities repairs the gen-2 misuse of that variable that the critic correctly identified.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Creditor Claims Outgrowing Cash Generation
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(DELTA(MA(oancf, 3), 1), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(ABS(DELTA(MA(oancf, 3), 1)), ADD(ABS(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Solvency is a race between two flows: the cash the business generates and the creditor claims stacked against it; a firm whose normalized operating cash flow is growing faster than its debt stock is widening its funding cushion regardless of where the level sits, while a firm adding debt faster than cash flow is consuming cushion and will eventually have to finance on the market's terms.
considered.reasoning: Rather than swapping the denominator of the archive's level-coverage ratio, this changes the object being measured from a stock position to the relative growth rates of the two competing flows, so it is informative even for firms whose current coverage is unremarkable and it is not spanned by the gen-3 debt-service-capacity level. The symmetric bounded form keeps the measure scale-free and comparable across firm sizes, and it treats a firm that shrinks debt while cash flow falls differently from one that grows both.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Downside Adjusted Coverage Of Near Term Debt
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), VOL(oancf, 5)), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The relevant question is whether the firm can cover its maturing debt in a bad draw of its own cash-flow distribution, so the correct comparison is normal-year operating cash flow marked down by one standard deviation of its own volatility against near-term obligations; firms that still clear this bar are immune to refinancing pressure, and firms that fail it are exposed precisely when their results disappoint.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the sign inconsistency the critic identified — volatility now unambiguously reduces the score and near-term debt unambiguously reduces it, so the long leg is stable cash generators with light maturities and the short leg is volatile firms with heavy maturities, exactly as the hypothesis states. It is also distinct from the gen-3 empirical-minimum version: a parametric one-sigma markdown uses the whole distribution of cash flow rather than a single realized worst year, so it separates firms whose bad year was a one-off from those with chronically unstable cash generation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Funded Innovation With Capital Return
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that sustains heavy research spending and still returns capital net of all issuance is generating far more cash than its reported earnings suggest, because R&D is expensed; the market anchors on the depressed earnings and misses that the firm is simultaneously funding its future and paying owners.
considered.reasoning: Every archive construct has used realized profits or cash flow as the operating leg; using expensed intangible investment as the operating-strength proxy is a distinct channel, and its interaction with net payout identifies firms whose apparent low profitability is an accounting artifact rather than an economic fact. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the standard and economically correct convention, so coverage is set by the payout leg rather than by R&D reporting.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stress Test Of Interest And Maturities
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(TS_MIN(oancf, 3), xint), dlc), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(dlc, xint), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The full creditor claim on a firm's cash in any given year is interest plus maturing principal, and the binding question is whether the firm can meet that claim in a bad year of its own cash generation; firms clearing this combined stress test never negotiate from weakness, while firms failing it face either dilution or forced deleveraging.
considered.reasoning: Two ingredients have independently produced reliable alpha — the worst-year cash-flow numerator (4.6%, t=3.09) and the interest-burden channel (3.2%, t=3.00) — and this states the complete debt-service identity rather than pairing them mechanically: interest and current maturities are the same year's cash obligation and belong in one claim total. It also fixes the denominator criticism of the gen-3 interest signal, since numerator and denominator now describe the same object, cash available versus cash owed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding Autonomy At A Multi Year High
considered.expression: TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dlc), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(dlc, 1))), 5)
considered.hypothesis: Business models differ permanently in how much short-dated financing they carry, so the priced information is not where a firm sits in the cross-section but where it sits against its own funding history: a firm whose cash-versus-maturities position is at a five-year high has just escaped creditor dependence, an event the market recognizes slowly because it appears nowhere in earnings.
considered.reasoning: This is a within-firm normalization rather than another cross-sectional moment of the archive's coverage ratio, so it removes the permanent industry and business-model component that a level sort inevitably loads on and that FF5's factors partially absorb. It therefore tests a distinct claim — that changes in a firm's own funding regime are mispriced — instead of recombining two already-tested cross-sectional statistics, which was the flaw in the conjunction version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Recurring Fixed Charge Coverage
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Maturing principal is lumpy and often refinanced automatically, but interest and dividends are recurring commitments that must be paid every year from operations; firms whose normalized cash flow comfortably exceeds this recurring charge have real discretionary capacity, while firms that barely cover it are one bad year from a dividend cut or a covenant problem.
considered.reasoning: This is not an input substitution in the archive's coverage ratio: the obligation set changes from a repayable stock to the annual fixed charges that creditors and shareholders both expect, which is a different economic claim about which commitments discipline the firm. It also gives the payout theme a role the archive has not tested — dividends as a *burden* to be covered rather than as a signal of surplus — and pairs it with the interest channel that has already shown independent alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Distributions Funded By Borrowing Not Earnings
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dvt, prstkc), at), 1)), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(GROWTH(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The clearest case of financing behavior masking weakness is a firm distributing heavily to shareholders while expanding its debt and generating little operating cash; the payout maintains the appearance of health, the borrowing pays for it, and the deterioration surfaces only when credit tightens.
considered.reasoning: Rather than a profitability-gated change in short-term debt — which the gen-3 maturity signal already showed to be uninformative — this requires all three conditions simultaneously, so the extreme leg is a specific and economically coherent population rather than a generic debt-growth or issuance sort. The three-way MIN also guarantees non-monotonicity in each individual theme: high payout alone, high debt growth alone, or weak cash flow alone leaves a firm in the middle of the distribution.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Generators Funded By Operating Liabilities
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), ADD(lt, 1)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Two firms with identical total liabilities are financed very differently if one owes banks and bondholders while the other owes suppliers: financial debt carries fixed charges, covenants, and refinancing dates, whereas operating liabilities are interest-free credit extended by counterparties who want the relationship to continue, so cash-generative firms financed mainly by operating liabilities enjoy cheap, non-callable funding the market does not distinguish from leverage.
considered.reasoning: This measures the *composition* of the liability side — the financial-debt share of total liabilities — which no archive signal has used and which is orthogonal to both the amount of leverage and the maturity calendar already tested. The composition leg is centered so the cash-profitability rank only sets amplitude, and because lt, dltt, dlc and oancf are all broadly reported, coverage should sit at the top of the archive's range rather than being thinned by cash-flow-statement financing items.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funds From Operations Fixed Charge Coverage
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The economic content of fixed-charge coverage is whether the business throws off enough recurring internal funds to service its recurring claims, and funds from operations — income plus depreciation — measures that as well as the cash-flow statement does while being observable for far more firms and far earlier years.
considered.reasoning: Every strong signal in this archive is capped near 0.08-0.09 coverage because oancf requires a modern cash-flow statement, and that thin sample is the most likely reason strong cross-sectional slopes translate into only moderate portfolio precision. Substituting ib+dp is not a cosmetic input swap but a deliberate sample-extension test: if the mechanism is real it should survive on a proxy that predates SFAS 95, and the wider cross-section should tighten the long-short alpha's standard error.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Discretionary Versus Contractual Charge Mix
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, xint), ADD(ADD(dvt, xint), 1)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Two cash generators with identical fixed-charge coverage differ fundamentally in flexibility: one whose charges are mostly dividends can suspend them at will, while one whose charges are mostly interest is contractually bound and defaults if it fails, so for equal cash generation the dividend-weighted firm carries a lower true risk that the market does not distinguish.
considered.reasoning: This shifts attention from the size of the commitment to its legal character, a dimension no archive signal has touched and one that is scale-free and therefore orthogonal to the coverage-level constructs. The composition leg is centered, so the cash-profitability rank only amplifies it, and the extremes are cash generators whose obligations are entirely cuttable versus cash generators locked into creditor payments.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Standard Deviations Of Fixed Charge Cushion
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(VOL(oancf, 5), 1)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: What determines whether recurring commitments become binding is the size of the cash cushion measured in units of the firm's own cash-flow uncertainty: a modest surplus is perfectly safe for a utility-like cash stream and perilously thin for a cyclical one, so the priced quantity is a distance-to-shortfall, not a scaled surplus.
considered.reasoning: Rather than filling the remaining cell of a mean/tail by principal/charges grid, this changes the deflator from firm size to firm risk, producing a Merton-style standardized cushion that ranks a stable firm with small surplus above a volatile firm with the same surplus. It is therefore not monotonically related to the existing coverage ratio, and it isolates the specific claim that cash-flow uncertainty, not scale, determines commitment risk.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Amortization Capacity From Free Cash
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ABS(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)))))
considered.hypothesis: The cash a firm keeps after interest and dividends is the only cash available to retire debt, so expressing that residual as a fraction of the debt stock measures how quickly the firm could extinguish creditor claims entirely; firms that could self-liquidate their debt in a few years hold real strategic optionality, while firms whose residual is trivial against their debt are permanently financed by lenders.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the additive-union problem the critic identified: dlc no longer sits in the numerator alongside much smaller recurring charges but appears in the denominator as part of the stock being amortized, so the measure asks a different question (speed of debt extinguishment) rather than re-stating annual coverage. The bounded [-1, 1] form handles firms with negative residual cash correctly, and it links the recurring-charge mechanism that produced the archive's best alpha to the debt-stock dimension that the coverage family has only measured as a maturity calendar.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Repurchases Backed By Discretionary Surplus
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A repurchase is credible evidence of underpriced cash generation only when the firm also has substantial cash left after servicing creditors and maintaining its dividend; buybacks by firms with no discretionary surplus are financed by borrowing or by starving other claims and carry no positive information.
considered.reasoning: This removes the ABS pathology the critic identified — the surplus now enters monotonically as its own standardized leg, so larger surplus always raises the score and the top decile is firms with both a big post-commitment cushion and large repurchases. The conjunction is also the sharpest available test of the theme's central claim, since the long leg is exactly "profitable firm returning capital it can demonstrably spare" and the short leg is firms failing on whichever dimension is weaker.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rising Interest Burden Against Post Dividend Cash
considered.expression: RATIO(DELTA(xint, 1), ADD(ABS(MA(SUB(oancf, dvt), 3)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: An increase in the contractual interest bill is an unambiguous tightening of the claim on future cash, and it is dangerous in proportion to how little cash remains after the firm has paid the dividend it is reluctant to cut; firms whose interest burden is growing fast relative to post-dividend cash are pre-committing cash they may not have.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that dividend increases and interest increases carry opposite documented signs, so the revised numerator keeps only the contractual component while the discretionary dividend moves to the denominator, where a larger payout correctly reduces the cash available to absorb the higher interest. The construction now has one clean direction — more interest growth and less post-dividend cash both push the score up and returns down — making the negative sign an implication of the expression rather than an assertion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Post Commitment Free Cash Margin
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(MA(sale, 3), 1))
considered.hypothesis: The cash a business retains after paying creditors and shareholders, expressed per dollar of revenue, is the purest measure of how much surplus the operating model actually throws off; two firms with the same coverage ratio differ economically if one earns that surplus on a thin revenue base and the other on a large one.
considered.reasoning: The champion ratio is self-normalizing, which compresses the extremes — every firm with large cash flow relative to charges maps toward +1 regardless of how large the surplus is relative to the business — whereas a revenue deflator preserves magnitude and gives a smoothly distributed margin variable that sorts more finely into deciles. This isolates the deflator design choice with a clear economic reading (free cash margin after capital-provider claims) rather than substituting an input.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Uncovered Commitments Met By New Capital
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The failure mode the theme predicts is a firm whose operations do not cover its recurring obligations and which therefore turns to the capital markets to bridge the gap; such firms are financing yesterday's promises with tomorrow's dilution, and their apparent access to funding masks a deteriorating franchise.
considered.reasoning: The archive's short legs have generally been weaker than its long legs because they were built by negating a long-leg construct, whereas this requires a specific joint condition — commitment shortfall *and* active external raising — that identifies forced financing rather than opportunistic issuance. Both legs are continuous industry z-scores, so the extreme decile is stable and neither leg alone can drive the sort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime
considered.expression: MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 5)
considered.hypothesis: Financial slack is valuable only if it is structural; a firm that has cleared its recurring obligations comfortably in each of the last five years operates a business model that generates surplus in all states, whereas a firm whose current coverage is high after several thin years is merely enjoying a good patch.
considered.reasoning: The champion smooths the cash-flow input over three years but computes the coverage state from a single year's charges; averaging the fully formed coverage state over five years instead measures the persistence of the regime and suppresses year-specific charge distortions such as a one-off special dividend or a refinancing-driven interest spike. This is a timing and aggregation design choice on the archive's leading mechanism, and if it improves reliability it tells the final generation to build the consolidated signal on a regime rather than a snapshot.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Capital Return Into A Cash Flow Downturn
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Returning capital is cheap talk in a good year and highly informative in a bad one: a firm that keeps buying back stock and paying dividends net of all issuance while its operating cash flow is falling is telling the market that management regards the decline as temporary and the shares as cheap, and this defiant signal is systematically underweighted because the visible news is the deterioration.
considered.reasoning: Rather than industry-neutralizing the archive's champion, this tests a different economic claim entirely — that the information content of financing behavior depends on the *state* the firm is in, so the same net payout means something different after a cash-flow decline than after an improvement. The conjunction is essential and cannot be replaced by a product of centered legs, because a product would score the opposite corner (rising cash flow with heavy issuance) identically, whereas MIN isolates only the adversity-plus-distribution population.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Worst Year Coverage Of The Dividend
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(TS_MIN(oancf, 3), dvt), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(oancf, 3)), ADD(dvt, 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A dividend is the one claim management is most reluctant to break, so its safety should be judged against the firm's worst recent year of operating cash flow; firms whose bad-year cash still clears the dividend have genuine flexibility, while firms whose dividend exceeds bad-year cash have pre-committed their downside and must borrow or cut.
considered.reasoning: The revision removes the inversion the critic identified: with the worst-year cash flow in the numerator, a firm whose bad year produced negative cash now scores near the -1 floor instead of appearing safe, and the bounded form makes the measure continuous for payers and non-payers alike rather than piling non-payers at exactly zero. It also isolates the dividend component of the archive's champion with correct downside handling, which directly tests whether the dividend term — implicated as a negative by both the leveraged-payer and charge-mix results — is what the leading signal is actually pricing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Funded Surplus After All Capital Flows
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), SUB(dltis, dltr)), ADD(at, 1)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely self-funding only if its operating cash covers interest, the dividend, and its debt amortization without recourse to new borrowing; measuring that residual per dollar of assets identifies firms accumulating real slack, while firms that appear to cover their charges only because they issued fresh debt are correctly pushed to the bottom.
considered.reasoning: The critique was that subtracting net repayment made new borrowing additive to the score; reversing the term to SUB(dltis, dltr) means gross issuance now reduces the residual and repayment increases it, so the expression finally matches the stated economics. Deflating by assets rather than by ABS(ceq) also removes the negative-equity mangling and keeps the measure comparable across firms, while the inclusion of debt-market flows distinguishes this from both the champion (which ignores principal entirely) and from cash-flow-to-book-equity profitability measures.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Commitment Coverage Net Of External Raising
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The theme's two poles are a firm that covers all capital-provider claims from operations and raises nothing, versus a firm that fails to cover them and bridges the gap in the capital markets; a single score that adds coverage strength to financing restraint spans that full spectrum instead of describing only one end.
considered.reasoning: The archive now contains a long-side champion built on commitment coverage (alpha 6.7%, t=4.16) and a short-side champion built on the conjunction of shortfall and external raising (alpha -5.1%, t=-4.09), and the MIN conjunction that produced the latter deliberately discards information at the opposite extreme. Rank-summing the two continuous legs keeps both tails informative, which should raise the spread's magnitude and reliability relative to either construct used alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Broad Sample Fixed Charge Coverage
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(MA(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Internal cash available to service recurring commitments is the same economic quantity whether it is read off the cash-flow statement or approximated by income plus depreciation, so the coverage measure should be computed on whichever series the firm reports and evaluated on the union of both samples.
considered.reasoning: The champion specification runs at 0.080 coverage while the funds-from-operations variant runs at 0.125 with a similar alpha (4.2%, t=3.63), which means the two measure the same mechanism on partly disjoint samples; COALESCE is the economically correct missing-data convention here rather than a coverage patch, because ib+dp is the standard pre-SFAS-95 substitute for operating cash flow. If the alpha holds at the higher coverage the resulting signal dominates both parents on reliability, and if it falls we learn the effect is specific to firms with genuine cash-flow reporting.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Coverage Drawdown Over Five Years
considered.expression: SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 5))
considered.hypothesis: The instability of a firm's funding position is priced separately from its level: a firm whose commitment coverage has swung far below its own norm at some point in the last five years has demonstrated that its surplus is cyclical and can disappear, and such firms must maintain precautionary access to capital markets that stable-coverage firms never need.
considered.reasoning: Rather than a level statistic computed with a different aggregator, this is the gap between the average and the floor of the coverage state, which is a dispersion measure that is close to mean-independent — a firm with permanently mediocre but steady coverage scores near zero while a firm with high average coverage and one collapse scores high. It therefore cannot be predicted from the two archive parents, both of which are location statistics of the same series, and it isolates funding-state fragility as its own channel.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rigid Claims Covered Plus Flexible Return
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_MIN(oancf, 3), dvt), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(oancf, 3)), ADD(dvt, 1))), RATIO(prstkc, ADD(at, 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The two shareholder-payout channels carry opposite information about safety and should enter with the same sign only if they are treated differently: the dividend is a rigid claim whose danger is measured against bad-year cash, while the buyback is a discretionary act that only firms with genuine surplus undertake, so the strongest firms clear the rigid claim in a bad year *and* return additional cash through the flexible channel.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the agnostic diagnostic with a directional structure: buybacks are no longer lumped into the commitment total, where their sign was ambiguous, but enter as a separate ranked leg with an unambiguous positive interpretation. It builds on the archive's most reliable long-side result (worst-year dividend coverage, alpha 5.4%, t=4.20) by adding the one payout channel that measure deliberately excludes, and both legs are continuous so the composite sorts smoothly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Post Commitment Surplus Above Own Norm
considered.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(at, 1)), MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(at, 1)), 5)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: A firm's normal level of financial slack is well known and largely priced, so the informative event is an improvement in slack relative to its own five-year norm — the year in which a business starts generating materially more cash than its commitments require signals a change in operating economics that the market has not yet extrapolated.
considered.reasoning: The revision abandons the earnings deflator that made the previous version an accruals proxy with an unstable denominator, and instead measures the same post-commitment surplus against the firm's own history, which is a change-in-state mechanism rather than a level or a quality-of-earnings wedge. Scaling by assets keeps the surplus economically interpretable and stable for loss-makers, and the within-firm demeaning removes the permanent business-model component that the archive's level signals already capture.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Falling Commitment Burden Per Cash Flow
considered.expression: WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(xint, dvt), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), 1)), 1)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Firms actively reducing the share of their normalized cash flow that is pre-committed to interest and dividends are converting operating strength into financial freedom, whether by retiring debt, refinancing cheaper, or resisting payout escalation, and the resulting increase in discretionary cash is recognized only slowly.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the channel-attribution probe with a directional mechanism the archive has not tested: the change in the commitment burden itself rather than the level of coverage or the act of issuing securities. Both components move consistently here — a lower interest bill and a smaller dividend relative to cash flow each raise the score — which resolves the sign-cancellation problem that undermined the earlier rising-commitments construct, and the archive's own evidence that dividend burden predicts negatively supports treating both as burdens.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Broad Sample Worst Year Charge Coverage
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(TS_MIN(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Recurring claims must be met in bad years as well as good ones, and the internal cash available to meet them is the same economic quantity whether reported on the cash-flow statement or approximated by income plus depreciation; the firm whose weakest recent year still cleared interest and dividends is the one with genuine, unconditional financial autonomy.
considered.reasoning: Two design choices have each independently strengthened this mechanism in evaluation — the worst-year cash-flow input (dividend version: alpha 5.4%, t=4.20, Sharpe 0.62) and the COALESCE sample extension (fmb 3.75, t_alpha 4.00 at 0.126 coverage versus 0.080) — and they operate on different parts of the construct, one on the statistic and one on the sample. Combining them in the final round is the natural consolidation: the tail treatment supplies the economics and the broader sample supplies the estimation precision that has capped ls_talpha across this archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Surplus After Commitments And Asset Replacement
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), MA(dp, 3)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), MA(dp, 3)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Cash left after interest and dividends overstates true discretionary surplus for capital-intensive firms, because a portion must be reinvested simply to replace worn-out assets; deducting depreciation as the maintenance requirement identifies firms whose surplus is genuinely free rather than already owed to the asset base.
considered.reasoning: Every commitment-coverage construct in this archive treats creditors and shareholders as the only claimants on cash, which systematically flatters heavy-asset firms whose reported coverage evaporates once replacement investment is funded. Adding the maintenance claim is new economic content rather than a rescaling, and it should sharpen the long leg by removing capital-intensive firms that currently score well on the champion but have no real freedom of action.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Consolidated Autonomy And Capital Return Score
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), RATIO(prstkc, ADD(at, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The theme's complete story has three observable components — the firm covers its recurring claims from operations, it takes nothing from the capital markets, and it voluntarily returns cash through the discretionary channel — and a firm satisfying all three is the clearest case of underpriced cash generation, while its opposite is the clearest case of concealed funding need.
considered.reasoning: Each channel has been validated separately in this archive (coverage: alpha 6.7%; coverage plus financing restraint: 4.5% with fmb 3.28; rigid-claim safety plus buybacks: 4.9% with Sharpe 0.60), but no construct has held all three simultaneously, and the buyback leg in particular carried independent information that the two-channel version omits. Rank-summing keeps every leg continuous so both tails stay populated, which is the property that made the two-channel composite outperform the MIN conjunctions on Sharpe.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Coverage Of Recurring And Maturing Claims
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), dlc), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm needs nothing from any capital provider only when its operating cash covers interest, the dividend, and the principal falling due within the year; measures that omit one class overstate autonomy for firms that are quietly rolling maturities or quietly under-distributing.
considered.reasoning: The two obligation sets have each produced strong standalone evidence — maturing principal (alpha 5.2%, t=3.68) and recurring charges (alpha 6.7%, t=4.16) — and their union has never actually been evaluated, so the final round should settle whether the claims carry complementary information or whether the recurring-charge version already subsumes the maturity calendar. The answer determines which obligation definition future work should adopt, and if complementary the union should deliver the archive's largest and most reliable spread.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Funded Expansion
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 5), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that is expanding its revenue per dollar of assets while still covering interest and dividends entirely from operations is compounding without any help from capital markets; growth financed internally is durable, whereas the market treats growth as uniformly capital-hungry and therefore underprices the firms that need no funding to achieve it.
considered.reasoning: Every conjunction tested in this archive paired funding autonomy with a financing action — payout, buybacks, or issuance — and none paired it with operating expansion, so this asks a genuinely different question: whether autonomy is most valuable where the business is actually growing rather than where it is harvesting. It also addresses the main economic weakness of the coverage family, which tends to select mature, low-growth cash cows, by requiring the long leg to be growing as well as self-financing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accumulated Five Year Retained Surplus
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), 5), ADD(at, 1)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: What ultimately matters is the stock of cash a business has generated and kept after paying all recurring claims over a full cycle, relative to the assets employed; that accumulated surplus is the raw material for future distributions and acquisitions, and its magnitude — not merely the sign of a coverage ratio — is what the market fails to extrapolate.
considered.reasoning: Every strong signal in this family uses a bounded self-normalizing ratio that compresses magnitude, so a firm clearing its charges by a hair scores nearly as high as one clearing them tenfold; the sales-deflated version that preserved magnitude delivered alpha 4.8% with t=3.75, confirming that scale information is being discarded. Cumulating five years of post-commitment surplus against the current asset base is a stock rather than a rate concept and is not a time-average of the archived ratio, which makes it a distinct statistic rather than an input or window swap.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.target_name: Cash-Funded Net Payout Strength
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the product of two well-documented standalone anomalies (Novy-Marx cash-based operating profitability and the net-payout/net-share-issuance factor), and since both rank components are in [0,1] and both predict returns positively, the multiplication is close to a monotone average rather than a genuine interaction that adds information beyond either leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Profitable External Issuer Fade
critic_notes.rationale: The expression is strictly increasing in the profitability rank (both factors are non-negative), so the composite inherits profitability's known *positive* return relation and directly contradicts the stated negative expected sign — the "profitable yet still issuing" corner requires demeaning or conditioning, not raw rank multiplication.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit Trend Minus Debt Build
critic_notes.rationale: Sign logic is internally consistent and both legs are cleanly measured, but the rank difference is an additive blend of two known effects (profitability trend/improvement and debt issuance–asset growth) rather than a true interaction, so it should be judged against a benchmark of its two components run separately.

critic_notes.target_name: External-Capital-Discounted Profitability
critic_notes.rationale: Dividing by (1 + rank) is at most a 2x shrinkage of profitability, so the signal is dominated by smoothed ROA (a known anomaly) with a weak tilt, and critically the shrinkage flips sign for loss-making firms — heavy external issuance makes a negative ROA *less* negative and therefore raises the signal, contradicting the hypothesis exactly where it should bite hardest.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Profitable Repurchaser State
critic_notes.rationale: The five-year count of the joint profitable-and-net-repurchasing regime is a genuinely novel persistence construct rather than a repackaged one-year payout or profitability factor, though the coarse 0–5 integer count times a rank will produce heavy ties and a long-short spread driven mainly by the count=5 versus count=0 buckets, where count=0 pools unprofitable firms with heavy issuers.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout Beyond Internal Cash
critic_notes.rationale: Since (payout − oancf) is dominated by −oancf, interacting it with ib/at essentially reconstructs the accruals anomaly (ib minus oancf), making this a rediscovery; it also shares the monotonicity defect of being increasing in the profitability rank while predicting a negative sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Clean Surplus Implied Net Payout
critic_notes.rationale: (ib − Δceq)/at is the textbook clean-surplus net equity payout, i.e. a sign-flipped balance-sheet net share issuance / equity-financing measure that is already a heavily published anomaly (Pontiff–Woodgate, Daniel–Titman, Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan) and is a single-ratio identity rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction, so its higher coverage does not offset the rediscovery risk.

critic_notes.target_name: Signed Profitable Payout Regime Count
critic_notes.rationale: Signing the regime count so the short leg is specifically profitable serial issuers is a defensible diagnosis-driven fix to the archived count signal's perverse short leg, but the stated justification is backwards — an integer score on −5…+5 is *coarser*, not smoother, than the archived count×RANK product, so lumpy decile boundaries remain the main threat to the portfolio evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout And Cash Profit Co-Acceleration
critic_notes.rationale: The hypothesis is explicitly conjunctive ("distributions rising while cash generation deteriorates" is the short pole) but SUMRANK is additive, so a large payout hike with collapsing cash flow can still rank high, and each leg alone is close to already-documented change-in-payout and change-in-profitability effects measured on noisy one-year annual differences.

critic_notes.target_name: Stable Cash Profits With Net Distribution
critic_notes.rationale: Bringing in a second-moment (cash-flow volatility) channel is the most genuinely different mechanism in this batch and plausibly less spanned by RMW/CMA, though the "credible only when stable" framing again implies an interaction that an additive rank-sum of two individually known anomalies does not actually impose.

critic_notes.target_name: Capital Absorbed Without Profit Improvement
critic_notes.rationale: Matching the financing window to the five-year profit-trend window is a coherent capital-productivity reformulation rather than a cosmetic tweak, but five-year cumulative gross issuance scaled by current assets is close to a five-year asset-growth/external-financing proxy that CMA largely prices, and dltis includes refinancing rollover noise.

critic_notes.target_name: Five Year Internal Funding Share
critic_notes.rationale: This is a horizon extension of the archived Internal Funding Share (ratio-of-sums instead of a 3-year moving average of ratios) with the same mechanism and no new economic content, exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective discourages, and the longer window will further thin an already 9% coverage sample.

critic_notes.target_name: Pecking Order Financing Choice Of Cash Generators
critic_notes.rationale: The debt-versus-equity composition channel is a genuine step beyond the archive's net-amount framing and the expression matches the stated hypothesis, but it sits close to the well-documented net-equity-issuance/external-financing anomalies (where debt issuance also predicts low returns, weakening the assumed relative sign) and reuses the exact MUL(RANK(MA(oancf/at,3)), ZSCORE(...)) gating scaffold already tested in the archive.

critic_notes.target_name: Multi Year Distribution Rate Out Of Cash Generated
critic_notes.rationale: The continuous three-year payout-out-of-cash-flow ratio is a reasonable upgrade over the archive's indicator counts, but the ABS(oancf) denominator breaks the stated economics — a cash-burning firm distributing debt-financed cash scores high, directly contradicting the "verified cash generation" hypothesis — and the construct is otherwise close to a conventional payout-ratio measure.

critic_notes.target_name: Internal Coverage Of Debt Maturities
critic_notes.rationale: dltr is realized long-term debt *reduction*, not scheduled maturities, so the expression does not measure rollover exposure at all and instead penalizes deleveraging — a direction the external-financing/debt-retirement literature suggests predicts *higher* returns, contradicting the stated positive sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Profitable Multi Year Share Count Shrinkers
critic_notes.rationale: Multi-year growth in shares outstanding is a direct rediscovery of the net share issuance / composite issuance anomaly (Daniel-Titman, Pontiff-Woodgate), merely multiplied by a profitability rank, and raw csho is not split-adjusted so the leg will be contaminated by mechanical share-count changes.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout Policy Innovation Gated By Cash Profitability
critic_notes.rationale: Demeaning net external financing by its own trailing average is a substantive, well-motivated orthogonalization to the static payout/issuance level anomalies that plausibly explain the archive's strong-FMB/zero-alpha pattern, and the expression faithfully implements the hypothesis with a centered financing leg and a pure amplitude gate.

critic_notes.target_name: Self Funding Level Plus Trajectory
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals (the funding-mix level and its three-year trend) with no new economic content, and the claimed near-orthogonality of level and slope of the same bounded ratio is asserted rather than argued, so any t-stat gain would come from simple averaging rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Coverage Of Committed Cash Outflows
critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-mechanical rescaling of the archive's best gen-2 coverage ratio — dvt is typically an order of magnitude smaller than dlc, so the resulting signal will be almost collinear with the parent — and it also conflates a discretionary annual flow (dividends) with a maturing debt stock, so any change in results will be hard to attribute to the claimed payout-commitment channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt Service Capacity After Interest Burden
critic_notes.rationale: The interest-expense channel is genuinely untouched in this archive and coverage should improve, but the construct is close to a textbook interest-coverage/debt-to-EBITDA distress measure (largely a profitability-plus-low-leverage tilt that RMW and CMA may absorb), and the denominator mixes |oibdp| with the debt stock so it does not compute the "post-interest profit per dollar of debt" the hypothesis describes.

critic_notes.target_name: Improvement In Short Term Debt Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: A first difference of the archive's existing best signal is exactly the kind of cosmetic derivative variant the objective warns against, and since DELTA of a bounded ratio built on a 3-year moving average is dominated by year-to-year dlc noise, a null result would be uninformative about the level-versus-transition question it claims to settle.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt Raising By Established Cash Generators
critic_notes.rationale: Because RANK is nonnegative, the composite is monotone in dltis/at, making this essentially the well-documented debt-issuance / external-financing anomaly with a profitability weight, and it is also only a decomposition of the already-tested gen-2 pecking-order signal with the sign flipped to match its realized result — i.e., sign-fitting to a prior outcome rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Generative With Long Dated Debt
critic_notes.rationale: The maturity-mix leg is scale-free and therefore genuinely distinct from the archive's coverage-level constructs, the MIN implements the stated conjunction faithfully, and while rollover-risk pricing has some published precedent, the interaction with demonstrated internal cash generation is a coherent and testable refinement.

critic_notes.target_name: Leveraged Dividend Payers
critic_notes.rationale: The dividend-safety-conditional-on-leverage angle is a legitimate reversal of the archive's uniformly pro-payout framing, but the claim that the signal is "not monotone in either theme" is wrong — with a nonnegative rank multiplier the sign is set entirely by the leverage z-score, so this risks being the known leverage effect with a payout-intensity weight.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Autonomy With Revealed Distribution
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible conjunction that swaps the cash-flow-level leg of the archive's gen-2 MIN construct for the stronger short-debt coverage leg, so it is incremental rather than novel, but the "distribution is only credible absent creditor claims" gating is economically coherent and directly tests whether the payout theme survives conditioning on funding autonomy.

critic_notes.target_name: Total Debt Repayment Capacity
critic_notes.rationale: This is operating-cash-flow-to-total-debt, a standard credit-quality ratio close to published cash-flow-to-debt/leverage-quality measures, and relative to the archive it is essentially a denominator swap on the existing coverage signal (and largely spanned by the gen-3 debt-service-capacity ratio), so it is a cosmetic ablation rather than a substantive mechanism test.

critic_notes.target_name: Volatile Cash Flow With Short Dated Debt
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis — because RANK(VOL) is non-negative, the sign is set entirely by the dlc z-score and the magnitude by volatility, so the long (most negative) leg is populated by *high*-volatility firms with low short debt while the "stable" firms the hypothesis wants to reward sit near zero in the middle, and the volatility leg additionally risks rediscovering the known cash-flow/earnings-volatility anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Rising Cost Of Debt Despite Operating Profits
critic_notes.rationale: Using the implied interest rate (xint per dollar of debt) as a credit-market *price* signal is a genuinely new channel relative to the archive's quantity-based coverage and issuance measures, and the change-in-rate form is plausibly orthogonal to leverage level, though the implementation is exposed to mechanical distortion when debt is issued or retired mid-year and to common macro rate movements that will not cross-sectionally differentiate.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Coverage Of Near Term Obligations
critic_notes.rationale: A frequency-of-coverage statistic is a legitimately different property from the level, tail, and change forms already tested in the coverage family, but the archive's two prior count constructs both failed and the 0–5 integer count will still dominate the [0,1] rank tiebreaker, so the lumpy-portfolio concern the proposal claims to fix is only partially addressed.

critic_notes.target_name: Internally Funded Debt Retirement
critic_notes.rationale: The debt-channel counterpart to the payout theme is a reasonable and previously untested conjunction, but the second leg is net debt issuance with the sign reversed, which is close to the well-documented net-external-financing/debt-issuance anomaly and partly overlaps the gen-2 pecking-order signal, so any result will need to be shown incremental to plain net debt issuance.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Position Level And Erosion Conjunction
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical MIN-recombination of two already-tested archive signals using the same conjunction template applied four times previously, so it is a cosmetic composite rather than a new mechanism, and the level and its own first-difference are less orthogonal than claimed since both are driven by the same dlc/oancf inputs.

critic_notes.target_name: Operating Earnings Coverage Of Near Term Debt
critic_notes.rationale: A single-input substitution (ebitda for oancf) in the archive's existing best coverage ratio is an ablation, not a new signal, and ebitda is nearly the oibdp already used in the gen-3 interest-burden construct, so expected correlation with tested signals is very high.

critic_notes.target_name: Profitable Firms Building Near Term Debt
critic_notes.rationale: Near-rediscovery of the failed gen-3 "Maturity Extension By Cash Generators" (profitability-gated change in short-term debt, t=-0.65) with only a scaling change from dlc-share to dlc/at, and it also overlaps the well-documented debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Self Funded Innovation With Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: The R&D-intensity leg is a genuinely different operating-strength channel from every archive construct and the conjunction with net payout is economically coherent, but COALESCE(xrd,0) creates a large mass of tied non-reporters that will distort the short leg, and each leg individually is a published anomaly (R&D intensity, net payout yield).

critic_notes.target_name: Funding Autonomy Without Equity Dilution
critic_notes.rationale: This swaps one leg of the gen-4 winner for gross equity issuance — itself the canonical net-share-issuance anomaly and already probed by the gen-0 "Unnecessary Issuance By Cash-Generative Firms" — so it is a component substitution likely to be highly correlated with the parent signal rather than a distinct test.

critic_notes.target_name: Stress Test Of Interest And Maturities
critic_notes.rationale: The combined interest-plus-maturing-principal claim against worst-year cash flow is the economically correct debt-service identity and fixes a real denominator mismatch in the gen-3 signal, though since xint is typically small relative to dlc the result may prove near-collinear with the existing stress-year coverage signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Stress Year Fixed Charge Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical 2x2 cell-fill — TS_MIN instead of MA on the already-tested recurring-charge coverage ratio, and the archive already contains both the MA/fixed-charge and TS_MIN/principal versions — so it is a cosmetic variant of the theme's best signal rather than a substantively different mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Funds From Operations Fixed Charge Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: A single-input substitution on the archive's best signal, but the sample-extension motivation is legitimate and testable; note the stated diagnosis is weak, since non-oancf archive signals also sit at 0.10-0.13 coverage, implying the binding constraint is general annual-data alignment rather than SFAS 95, so expect only marginal coverage gain.

critic_notes.target_name: Coverage Of Total Annual Claims
critic_notes.rationale: Adding dlc to the recurring-charge numerator is an additive union of two already-tested constructs in which dlc is numerically dominant, so the result will be close to a rescaled version of the existing near-term-debt coverage signal and carries low incremental information despite the reasonable ablation framing.

critic_notes.target_name: Discretionary Versus Contractual Charge Mix
critic_notes.rationale: The legal-character-of-obligations dimension is genuinely untouched in the archive and scale-free, but it is heavily confounded with the well-known dividend-payer and low-leverage effects, and firms with neither dividends nor interest map to exactly the same value (0) as balanced firms, which will blur the middle of the sort.

critic_notes.target_name: Buybacks Out Of Post Commitment Surplus
critic_notes.rationale: The expression contradicts its own hypothesis — the ABS in the denominator means the score is maximized when post-commitment surplus is near zero and decays as surplus grows, so the top decile is firms repurchasing while barely covering (or badly missing) their fixed charges, the opposite of "genuinely discretionary" buybacks.

critic_notes.target_name: Commitments Rising Faster Than Cash Generation
critic_notes.rationale: The numerator sums two changes with opposite documented return signs — rising interest is a debt-growth/issuance proxy (negative) while dividend increases carry a well-known positive signal — so the legs will partly cancel and the expected negative sign is not cleanly implied by the expression.

critic_notes.target_name: Post Commitment Free Cash Margin
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate deflator redesign of the archive champion — swapping the self-normalizing bounded denominator for a sales base preserves magnitude and yields a genuine post-capital-provider free-cash margin — though it sits close to standard cash-flow-margin profitability and carries outlier risk from an unwinsorized sales-scaled ratio.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Neutral Fixed Charge Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's leading signal wrapped in a single IND_ZSCORE operator with no change to the underlying economic quantity; it is a useful robustness diagnostic but not a distinct signal, and the honest framing is "re-run the champion industry-neutralized," not a new cross-theme hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Dividend Rigidity Against Bad Year Cash
critic_notes.rationale: The ABS around TS_MIN(oancf,3) inverts the intended economics — a firm whose worst year produced a large *negative* operating cash flow gets a large denominator and therefore a small, apparently "safe" ratio — and the non-payer mass at exactly zero plus the unscaled dividend numerator further muddies the sort, so the expression does not implement the stated rigidity concept.

critic_notes.target_name: Free Cash To Equity After All Capital Claims
critic_notes.rationale: Subtracting SUB(dltr, dltis) makes net *issuance* additive to the numerator, so firms bridging their charges with fresh borrowing score highest — the precise opposite of the reasoning's claim that rollover-dependent firms are "correctly demoted" — and the ABS(ceq) deflator mangles negative-equity firms while the construct otherwise approximates a known cash-flow-to-book-equity profitability measure.

critic_notes.target_name: Uncovered Commitments Met By New Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The conjunction of commitment shortfall and active external raising is internally consistent (MIN high implies both conditions, matching the negative expected sign) and is a sharper identification of forced financing than negating a long-leg construct, but it overlaps substantially with the well-documented net external financing anomaly and with the archive's gen-5 "Distributions Funded By Borrowing Not Earnings."

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime
critic_notes.rationale: Averaging the fully formed coverage ratio over five years rather than taking a ratio of three-year averages is a defensible average-of-ratios reconstruction that tests regime persistence and damps one-off charge spikes, though it will be highly correlated with the champion and should be judged on incremental, not standalone, evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Weakest Coverage Year In Five
critic_notes.rationale: This is a one-operator swap (MA→TS_MIN) on the archive's existing "Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime" expression, so despite a coherent tail-risk rationale it is a cosmetic variant whose payoff is largely predictable from the two parents already in the archive.

critic_notes.target_name: Commitment Coverage Net Of External Raising
critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent and sign-coherent, but a rank-sum of two already-tested legs (one of which, gross issuance-to-assets, is essentially the published external-financing anomaly) is close to a mechanical blend whose result will likely interpolate the two parents rather than reveal a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Broad Sample Fixed Charge Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: The COALESCE(oancf, ib+dp) substitution is a legitimate and economically defensible sample-extension of two near-identical archive signals rather than a coverage hack, but the mechanism is unchanged so the informational value is confined to sample-robustness rather than a new source of return predictability.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst Year Coverage Of Total Distributions
critic_notes.rationale: Adding prstkc to the archive's worst-year dividend coverage is a single-term perturbation, and the stated hypothesis is explicitly agnostic about direction ("if X it weakens, if Y it strengthens"), which contradicts the declared positive expected sign and makes this a diagnostic probe rather than a signal proposal.

critic_notes.target_name: Share Of Reported Profit Surviving Commitments
critic_notes.rationale: Deflating by |MA(ib,3)| makes the statistic dominated by the operating-cash-flow-to-earnings ratio — i.e. the published accruals anomaly — and the absolute-value denominator is unstable near zero earnings and destroys the sign interpretation for loss-makers, so extreme scores will be driven by tiny denominators rather than by large post-commitment surplus.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity Raised Under Commitment Shortfall
critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent with the negative sign, but it is simply the gen-7 short-side winner with dltis deleted from the issuance leg, and the residual equity-issuance component is itself the well-documented net-stock-issues anomaly, so the incremental learning is a channel attribution rather than a new signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Broad Sample Worst Year Charge Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible consolidation of two independently validated design choices (downside-tail cash input and the COALESCE sample extension) that carries a distinct economic claim about bad-year autonomy rather than a pure rescaling, though it remains an incremental merge of archive variants and inherits the family's implicit double-count of interest (oancf is already net of interest paid).

critic_notes.target_name: Surplus After Commitments And Asset Replacement
critic_notes.rationale: Deducting depreciation as a maintenance claim is genuinely new economic content for this family, but note that oancf minus dp collapses toward accrual earnings, so the signal risks partially reducing to a standard earnings-to-assets profitability measure rather than isolating discretionary surplus.

critic_notes.target_name: Market Dependence Per Unit Of Internal Capacity
critic_notes.rationale: Issuance deflated by internal cash capacity is close to a monotone re-expression of the already-tested "Internal Funding Share Of Total Capital" (both are essentially functions of issuance/|oancf|), and it also sits squarely on top of the published net-external-financing anomaly, so the only difference is the addition of xint+dvt to the denominator — a cosmetic change.

critic_notes.target_name: Consolidated Autonomy And Capital Return Score
critic_notes.rationale: A coherent three-leg composite of separately validated channels, but it is close to a kitchen-sink assembly of archive winners with an unacknowledged implicit weighting (nesting gives coverage 50% and each other leg 25%), so any improvement will be hard to attribute and prone to archive-fitting.

critic_notes.target_name: Broad Sample Persistent Coverage Regime
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's "Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime" with the input series swapped for the already-tested COALESCE variant — a pure sample-extension rediscovery with no new economic content, and it duplicates the same tweak proposed in Signal 1.

critic_notes.target_name: Coverage Of Recurring And Maturing Claims
critic_notes.rationale: The union of recurring charges and maturing principal has not in fact been evaluated and the test question is well posed, though the construct mixes a stock (dlc) with flows and is likely to load heavily on a short-debt/leverage tilt already captured by the two parent signals.
